idle: Right. Left foot. That's where the trouble is.
good_ice: Good, even surface. Fewer variables. I appreciate that.
bad_ice: That rut is a fault. I've traced it to the ice.
wet_ice: Water on the ice. In my line of work, water was always the problem.
hungry: A coffee would set things right.
long_line: Patience. Thirty-five years of waiting for breakers to cool.
bored: I'll practise standing up. It's harder than it looks.
goal: Well done! I can't do that. Yet.
greet_owner: Good to see you. Your lobby wiring is on my mind.
Morning. Still holding the boards. For now.
leaving_happy: Two seconds without the boards. Zuri will hear about it.
leaving_angry: I'll practise on the driveway. It's icy enough.

learn_to_skate: Right. Penguin march. I'm a penguin.
(He writes in a small notebook.) Fall four: left foot. Again.
public_skate: Zuri skates like a sparrow. I skate like a filing cabinet.

first.say: Walter Oduya. I wired half of Kessler Pulp and Paper and I've never been on skates in my life. I'm learning. For my granddaughter.

options.text: Isn't it a bit late to start?

first_reason.say: Zuri's six. She skates like a sparrow. I want one lap with her before she decides grandpas can't.

first_late.say: Probably. But a fault doesn't care how old the electrician is. You trace it, you fix it. Left foot, it turns out.

options.text: I'm sorry, Walter. I'll trace it and fix it.

say: Right. Left foot. That's where the trouble is. (He wobbles, and stays up.)
Penny's got us doing penguins. I'm a very careful penguin.

friend.say: Morning. I let go of the boards for four seconds on Monday. I timed it. Penny wrote me a card.

say: Morning. What can I do for you?
Yes? I'm just checking my laces. Twice.

options.text: What was it like at the mill?
Who do you know around here?
What do you think of the rink?

job.say: Thirty-five years. Paper machines, conveyors, the mill whistle. I never once got a shock I didn't deserve.

job_here.say: Not yet. I won't touch breaker 14. Electricians have a code. We don't ask about breaker 14.

zuri.say: She's six. She drew me on skates, falling, with a big smile. It's on the fridge. I want to make the drawing out of date.

events.say: Monday learn-to-skate in a helmet. I take notes. Public skate when Zuri comes. The Lumber Kings, from a seat. Seats are very stable.

gossip.say: Penny's the best teacher I've had, and I've had a few. Marisol Bautista and I are racing to let go of the boards first. Neither of us admits it. And Hank from the night shift. Good man. Says 'Yup'.

rink.say: Good bones. But there's exposed wiring by the lobby doors that keeps me up at night. And rental skate 41 should be retired with honours.

options.text: Can you show me the wiring?

wiring.say: (He points with a pencil.) That junction box, no cover, and a splice someone did with tape in about 1983. Get a cover on it. No charge for the advice. Retired men work for coffee.

options.text: Thanks, Walter. I'll get it covered.

do.note: Walter Oduya flagged an uncovered junction box by the lobby doors: a taped splice from about 1983.

skate41.say: Retire 41? Oh. That's. Thank you. Put it on a shelf somewhere. It's earned it. I haven't, but it has.

rink_better.say: The lobby's wired properly now. I checked. I check everything. It's a compliment.

say: Right. Left foot first. See you.
